records.region: Southwest Greenland, inland-ice and exposed-rock corridor east of inner Ameralik
records.candidate_name_role: No representative natural-river hydronym is supported for the complete selected ice, exposed-rock and receiving-fjord composite.
records.naming_scope_hold_reason: The selected ice-margin, exposed-rock and historical inner Ameralik receiving sequence has complete ordinary terrain correspondence, but no whole natural-river hydronym is established. Ameralik is a bounded fjord label only.
records.completion_scope: Completed ordinary selected geographic correspondence and null whole-natural-river naming determination; no registry verification or modern hydraulic investigation.

scope_limits: The historical national geological map supports the complete ordinary ice, rock, lower passage and fjord setting; this is not proof that the modeled composite is one continuous natural river.
Ameralik names the bounded receiving fjord. No glacier name, river alias or scalar name is inferred from geographic proximity.
Thin blue thematic lines and Inland Ice contours do not establish surface or subglacial hydraulic continuity. No selected lake-throughflow or modern glacier-front claim is made.

Both fragments remain mainstem, at stages3 and2 respectively. Their join is not a tributary mouth. Only FID8906 carries supplied terminal metadata, whose sea class is preserved without claiming a surveyed contemporary river mouth.

The source and rendered ending positions are distinct. National-map scale and epoch do not establish their exact present-day bank, ice or water status. Formal registry verification, Korean name and all application flags remain unset or false.

bounded_name_observations.relationship: Printed name on the broader receiving water west of the selected lower pale corridor and inner ending. Bounded fjord context only; neither a selected whole-river name nor a river alias.

records.completion_scope: Completed ordinary selected geographic correspondence and null whole-natural-river naming determination; no registry verification or modern hydraulic investigation.

scope_limits: Complete ordinary ice, nunatak, exposed-rock and receiving-fjord correspondence does not establish one continuous natural river. No whole-route river hydronym is supported; local streams are not declared officially unnamed.
Gåsefjord and Nertiit Kangersivat are directly printed receiving-water labels. They remain bounded geographic observations, with no formal naming-register or whole-river alias claim.

The original is historical national-scale geological/glaciological mapping. Surface contours and ice-thickness information are not watercourse lines, current glacier fronts or proof of surface/subglacial hydraulic continuity.

Source and rendered endpoints are separately accounted for. Their small difference is not resolved into exact present land/ice/water placement; the supplied sea class is preserved metadata, not a surveyed river-mouth determination.

No selected tributary is present, no tributary endpoint is promoted to the mainstem ending, and no selected lake-throughflow or modern hydraulic behavior is established. Accepted, scalar and Korean names remain null; registry and application flags remain false.

publication_boundary: Own factual name/scope findings, public official URLs, bounded geometry metadata and public continuity pins only. research_order.progress_rule: Follow the actual continental order: Americas, Asia, Africa, Europe, then other, with all rivers before lakes. Preserve original queue IDs and ranks for continuity; apply documented geographic deferrals without counting them as name research, and place deferred objects into their corrected later phase by length-descending, stable-ID order. Prior candidate and scope-held assessments remain unresolved where stated.
